questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: As I live in Copenhagen, I had a wish to study in a smaller city and thus be closer to the nature that I am studying and reading about every day. Furthermore, Uppsala has a long history of botanic which is what I am interested in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy to get information, and I had all information that I needed when I left for Sweden.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't receive any assistance, because I didn't arrive on the official welcome day.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy because there is a collaboration between the university and the housing office.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is great! Rackarbergsgatan was the perfect place to stay!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was easy and they were very helpful. I got all information at the service desk in one of the university buildings.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They helped me both changing subjects but also just the first sign up when arriving. The first time was online due to covid, so I needed a Studium account to attend the classes, which was easy to figure out.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was registered for the classes I wished automatically by the university.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is easy to figure out, and most is done automatically when you wish for classes when applying to the university. It is, however, important to remember to sign up for the exams in time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had 3 different courses, and 2 of them were very good, whilst one was medium (perhaps because it was online).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was the same as at my home university. However, it was challenging in other ways that I am used to. The exams were easier, I would say, but the courses were challenging in other ways and it was necessary to attend and be well prepared.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were much more classes, and a lot more components to each course. This I really liked. Instead of the exam being the most important, there were many different parts to attend in order to pass the course. Also there were literature and ethics seminars which were very enlightening, and something that is not usually a part of the course at my home university.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Plant Structure and Function (15 ECTS)
Evolution of Life in the History of Earth (7.5 ECTS)
Marine Biology (15 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Marine biology had a 3 weeks field course on the West coast which was amazing. Here you really get experience and get to see what you are otherwise learning about. 
Also, Evolution of Life in the History of Earth, which is an evening course was very interesting. I would definitely recommend it!

questions.answer: The prices were very similar to the danish prices in general.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Uppsala has a very active student life with the student nations that offers numbers things to do every day.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many different things, it is just to find the right student nation and then you can find people who share your interests or learn something new.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the sewing club and the painting club at my student nation. In general I would just recommend you to join a student nation.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on a hike in the area, go see the botanical garden or the tropical green house. Also the museum at Evolutions Biologisk Centrum (EBC) is nice and free if you are a student.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, especially as Denmark and Sweden are quite similar.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the student nations and some activities in the welcome weeks where there is a lot planned. Don't be afraid to attend activities alone as everyone are joining to meet new people and find friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not any in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Very sweet and caring people and society in general.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Use the nature around you! It is amazing (I even saw northern lights in Uppsala).
Join a student nation!
Try the different reading halls in both libraries and university buildings. They are beautiful and very different.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Importance of signing up for the exam in the right time. As this is your own responsibility, you are not able to attend the exam if you forget.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
I enjoyed meeting a lot of sweet people, and having great talks and discussions about our cultural differences. 
The nature around Uppsala was beautiful and I really enjoyed hiking and spending time outside.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Attending social activities alone was very challenging in the beginning, however it was also a very empowering feeling when it was a good experience.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
